name: Practice Paper 3
subtitle: RRB Radiographer / X-Ray Technician — Full CBT Mock (Moderate–Tough)

subsections.title: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The foramen magnum is located in which bone?
questions.explanation: The spinal cord passes through the foramen magnum of the occipital bone, which is shown on Towne's view.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The right and left coronary arteries arise from the:
questions.explanation: They arise from the aortic sinuses just above the aortic valve cusps.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The tracheal bifurcation (carina) lies at approximately the level of:
questions.explanation: The sternal angle (of Louis) marks T4/T5, where the trachea divides.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The pylorus connects the:
questions.explanation: The pyloric sphincter controls emptying of the stomach into the duodenum.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The head of the femur articulates with the:
questions.explanation: The hip joint is a ball-and-socket joint between the femoral head and the acetabulum.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which carpal bone is a sesamoid bone lying within the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris?
questions.explanation: The pea-shaped pisiform lies on the triquetrum within the FCU tendon.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which is the largest paranasal sinus?
questions.explanation: The maxillary sinus (antrum of Highmore) is the largest and is best seen on Waters view.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: How many bronchopulmonary segments are there in the right lung?
questions.explanation: The right lung has 10 segments (3 upper, 2 middle, 5 lower).

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The spleen lies in relation to which ribs on the left side?
questions.explanation: The spleen lies under ribs 9–11 in the left hypochondrium, so lower left rib fractures can rupture it.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: In adults, the spinal cord usually ends at the level of:
questions.explanation: This is why lumbar puncture is done below this level, at L3–L4 or L4–L5.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which tarsal bone has no muscle attachments?
questions.explanation: The talus is largely covered with articular cartilage and has no muscle attachments.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The total blood volume of a normal adult is about:
questions.explanation: Blood volume is about 7–8% of body weight, roughly 5 L in a 70-kg adult.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: An X-ray tube is operated at 100 kVp. What is the maximum energy of the X-ray photons produced?
questions.explanation: The maximum photon energy in keV equals the peak kilovoltage. The average energy is about one-third to one-half of this.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: What is the minimum wavelength of X-rays produced at 124 kVp? (λ in nm = 1.24 / E in keV)
questions.explanation: λmin = 1.24/124 = 0.01 nm (Duane–Hunt law).

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The K-shell binding energy of tungsten is approximately:
questions.explanation: Tungsten K-characteristic X-rays (~59–69 keV) appear only when the tube is operated above about 70 kVp.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: An exposure of 200 mA for 0.1 second gives:

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: How many heat units (HU) are produced by a single-phase exposure of 80 kVp, 100 mA and 0.5 s?
questions.explanation: HU = kVp × mA × s = 80 × 100 × 0.5 = 4,000. (For three-phase and high-frequency generators, a factor of 1.35–1.41 is applied.)

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: According to the '15% rule', increasing kVp by 15% has about the same effect on film density as:
questions.explanation: +15% kVp ≈ 2 × mAs. The 15% rule is used to cut exposure time or patient dose.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: After passing through three half-value layers, the intensity of an X-ray beam is reduced to:

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Reducing the anode target angle results in:
options: A larger effective focal spot and less heel effect
No change in focal spot size
A smaller effective focal spot but a more pronounced heel effect
questions.explanation: A smaller angle gives finer detail but reduces field coverage and increases the heel effect.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Tube current (mA) in an X-ray tube is controlled mainly by:
questions.explanation: A higher filament current heats the filament more, which releases more electrons and increases tube mA.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The autotransformer in an X-ray circuit:
options: Works on self-induction with a single winding and is used to select kVp
Has two separate windings and steps voltage up to kilovolts
questions.explanation: The autotransformer supplies an adjustable voltage to the primary of the high-tension transformer.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: A high-tension transformer has a turns ratio of 1 : 500. If 200 V is applied to the primary, the secondary voltage is:

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Which interaction involves no loss of photon energy and no ionisation, and occurs mainly below about 10 keV?
questions.explanation: The photon is only redirected; its energy and wavelength are unchanged.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The relationship between half-value layer (HVL) and the linear attenuation coefficient (μ) is:
questions.explanation: From I = I₀e^(−μx), setting I = I₀/2 gives x = ln2/μ = 0.693/μ.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Compared with an 8 : 1 grid, a 12 : 1 grid:
options: Removes less scatter and needs a lower exposure
Removes more scatter but needs a higher exposure and more accurate centring
Has no effect on patient dose
Can be used at any FFD without cut-off
questions.explanation: A higher grid ratio cleans up scatter better, but it raises the Bucky factor (dose) and narrows the positioning latitude.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The 'air-gap technique' reduces scattered radiation reaching the image by:
questions.explanation: Obliquely scattered photons miss the receptor across the gap. Used in lateral C-spine and magnification radiography.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The inherent filtration of an X-ray tube is mainly provided by the:
options: Aluminium sheets added at the collimator
Glass envelope, insulating oil and tube window
questions.explanation: Inherent filtration is about 0.5–1 mm Al equivalent. Added filtration brings the total up to at least 2.5 mm Al.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: In a true lateral skull projection:
options: The interpupillary line is parallel to the IR
The median sagittal plane is perpendicular to the IR
The interpupillary line is perpendicular to the IR and the median sagittal plane is parallel to it
The orbitomeatal line is at 37° to the IR
questions.explanation: This avoids rotation and tilt so that the two halves of the skull superimpose exactly.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: In the Waters (occipitomental) projection, the orbitomeatal line forms an angle of about ___ with the image receptor.
questions.explanation: With a 37° OML angle (mentomeatal line perpendicular), the petrous ridges are projected just below the maxillary sinuses.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For Towne's (AP axial) projection, the central ray is angled:
questions.explanation: If the IOML is used as the baseline, the angle becomes 37° caudad.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For the PA axial (Caldwell) projection of the skull, the central ray is angled:
questions.explanation: This projects the petrous ridges into the lower third of the orbits.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The 'frog-leg' lateral projection of the hips is contraindicated in:
options: Suspected fracture of the femoral neck
questions.explanation: The position needs abduction and external rotation of the hip, which can displace a fracture.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: Judet's (45° oblique) projections of the pelvis are used to demonstrate the:
questions.explanation: The obturator oblique and iliac oblique views show the acetabular columns and rims.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For a lateral lumbar spine projection, the central ray is directed to:
options: The level of L3 (about 4 cm above the iliac crest) at the mid-coronal plane
The level of the symphysis pubis
questions.explanation: L3 lies at about the lower costal margin. Centring there covers L1–S1.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: In an AP shoulder projection with the arm externally rotated, which structure is seen in profile laterally?
questions.explanation: External rotation shows the greater tubercle laterally; internal rotation shows the lesser tubercle medially.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For a lateral projection of the elbow, the elbow is flexed to:
questions.explanation: With 90° flexion, a true lateral elbow shows the fat pads and the three concentric arcs.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: Bone age assessment is routinely done with a radiograph of the:
questions.explanation: The Greulich–Pyle atlas is based on PA radiographs of the left hand and wrist.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: Robert's method (AP thumb) best demonstrates the:
questions.explanation: The forearm is hyperpronated so that the dorsal surface of the thumb rests on the IR.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: Bilateral AP views of the acromioclavicular joints are taken with and without weights to demonstrate:
questions.explanation: Weights (5–8 lb) hanging from the wrists increase the gap at an injured AC joint.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The tunnel (Holmblad / Camp–Coventry) projection of the knee demonstrates the:
questions.explanation: It shows loose bodies and osteochondral defects in the intercondylar notch.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The sternum is radiographed in the RAO position (15°–20°) mainly to:
options: Separate the sternum from the clavicles
Project the sternum over the homogeneous heart shadow, clear of the vertebrae
Reduce the dose to the breasts only
Avoid using a long exposure time
questions.explanation: The heart provides a uniform background; a breathing technique blurs the overlying lung markings.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The zygomatic arches are best demonstrated by the:
questions.explanation: The SMV with reduced exposure shows the arches free of overlap, like jug handles.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: A 'horizontal beam' is used for the lateral knee in trauma mainly to demonstrate:
questions.explanation: A fat–fluid level in the suprapatellar bursa indicates an intra-articular fracture.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The slope of the straight-line portion of the characteristic (H&D) curve indicates the film's:
questions.explanation: A steeper slope means higher contrast and narrower latitude.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: If a processed radiograph transmits 1% of the incident light, its optical density is:
questions.explanation: OD = log₁₀(I₀/It) = log₁₀(100) = 2.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: In a 90-second automatic processor, the developer temperature is typically about:
questions.explanation: Higher temperature allows rapid development. Manual processing uses about 20 °C for 5 minutes.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: Which method is commonly used to recover silver from used fixer?
questions.explanation: An electric current plates the silver onto a cathode. Metallic replacement (steel wool) is another method.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: A direct-conversion flat-panel detector uses which material to convert X-rays straight into an electrical charge?
questions.explanation: Indirect detectors use a CsI or Gd₂O₂S scintillator with amorphous-silicon photodiodes.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: Quantum mottle (noise) in a radiographic image is mainly caused by:
questions.explanation: Too few photons give statistical fluctuation, which appears as a grainy image. Raise the mAs to reduce it.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: In digital or CT image display, increasing the window width will:
options: Decrease image contrast (more grey shades shown)
questions.explanation: A wide window (e.g., lung or bone) shows a long grey scale; a narrow window gives high contrast. Window level controls brightness.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: Reciprocity law failure in film-screen radiography occurs mainly with:
options: Very long or very short exposure times
questions.explanation: The same mAs does not always give the same density when screen light intensity is extreme.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Which of the following is a stochastic effect of radiation?
questions.explanation: For stochastic effects the probability rises with dose and there is no threshold. Deterministic effects have a threshold.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: According to the law of Bergonié and Tribondeau, which cells are the most radiosensitive?
questions.explanation: Cells that divide rapidly and are less differentiated are the most radiosensitive.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: The whole-body LD50/30 for humans (without medical treatment) is about:
questions.explanation: About 3–4 Gy kills 50% of an exposed population within 30 days.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: OSL (optically stimulated luminescence) dosimeters use:
questions.explanation: When stimulated by a laser, OSL material releases light proportional to the dose absorbed.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Non-ionic iodinated contrast media cause fewer adverse reactions than ionic media mainly because they have:
options: Higher iodine content per molecule only
questions.explanation: Low-osmolar agents cause less fluid shift, pain, heat sensation and fewer reactions.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Water-soluble contrast (e.g., Gastrografin) is preferred over barium when there is suspected:
questions.explanation: Barium leaking into the peritoneum causes severe peritonitis. Water-soluble contrast is absorbed.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Hysterosalpingography is ideally performed:
options: Between the 7th and 10th day of the menstrual cycle, after bleeding stops
Around the 25th day of the cycle
questions.explanation: This avoids irradiating an early pregnancy and avoids pushing endometrial tissue into the tubes.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Lipiodol, an oil-based iodinated contrast, is classically used in:
questions.explanation: Oily contrast must never be given intravenously. Its uses include lymphangiography and TACE.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: The most common arterial puncture site for diagnostic angiography by the Seldinger technique is the:
questions.explanation: The femoral artery is large and superficial, and can be compressed over the femoral head. The radial artery is increasingly used for cardiac work.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: If iodinated contrast extravasates during an IV injection, the immediate step is to:
options: Continue injecting faster to finish the dose
Stop the injection, elevate the limb and apply a cold compress
Apply a tight tourniquet above the site
questions.explanation: Most extravasations settle with conservative care. Large volumes or compartment signs need surgical review.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: In helical CT, pitch is defined as:
options: Number of detector rows × slice thickness
Table movement per rotation ÷ total beam collimation
questions.explanation: Pitch > 1 means faster coverage and lower dose but more gaps; pitch < 1 means overlapping data.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Beam-hardening artefact on a head CT appears as:
options: Dark streaks between dense bony structures (e.g., petrous bones)
Bright halo around the whole image
questions.explanation: Low-energy photons are filtered out in dense bone, so the beam's mean energy rises and the area beyond appears falsely dark (Hounsfield bar). Ring artefacts mean a detector fault.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: The Larmor frequency of hydrogen protons in a 1.5 T MRI scanner is about:
questions.explanation: f = γB = 42.58 MHz/T × 1.5 T ≈ 63.9 MHz. At 3 T it is about 127.7 MHz.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: A T1-weighted MR image is obtained with:
questions.explanation: T1W uses short TR and short TE; T2W uses long TR and long TE; PD uses long TR and short TE. Fat is bright on T1.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: In the ACR MRI safety zoning, Zone IV is the:
questions.explanation: Zone IV is the magnet room, where the field is always on and only screened persons may enter.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: The average speed of sound in soft tissue, assumed by ultrasound machines, is:
questions.explanation: Depth is calculated from the echo time using 1540 m/s. Sound is about 330 m/s in air and about 4080 m/s in bone.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: The radiotracer most widely used in PET imaging is:
questions.explanation: FDG is a glucose analogue, so tumours with high metabolism take up more of it.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: The two standard views in screening mammography are:
questions.explanation: The MLO view shows the most breast tissue, including the axillary tail.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Integral Coach Factory (ICF) of Indian Railways is located at:
questions.explanation: ICF is in Chennai, RCF in Kapurthala, MCF in Rae Bareli and BLW in Varanasi.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Banaras Locomotive Works (formerly Diesel Locomotive Works) is situated in:
questions.explanation: Chittaranjan has CLW (electric locomotives) and Patiala has PLW (formerly DMW).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Constitutional status was given to Panchayati Raj institutions by the:
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX (Panchayats). The 74th Amendment covers Municipalities.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: A 'Money Bill' is defined in which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 112 covers the Annual Financial Statement, Article 356 President's Rule and Article 280 the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: It was launched on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session, with the call 'Do or Die'.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: India and Sri Lanka are separated by the:
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Wular (J&K) is the largest freshwater lake. Chilika is a brackish-water lagoon.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: National Sports Day (29 August) is celebrated on the birth anniversary of:
questions.explanation: Dhyan Chand, the hockey legend, was born on 29 August 1905.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented in India from:
questions.explanation: GST was introduced by the 101st Constitutional Amendment and launched on 1 July 2017.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is in:
questions.explanation: WHO was established on 7 April 1948, now observed as World Health Day.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours and pipe B can empty it in 15 hours. If both are opened together, the empty tank will be filled in:
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30 per hour, so it takes 30 hours.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.explanation: 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, so the single discount is 28%.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How long will the boat take to travel 36 km downstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 18 km/h, and 36/18 = 2 hours.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A father is three times as old as his son. After 15 years he will be twice as old as his son. What is the father's present age?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: What is the LCM of 12, 18 and 30?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: If TUBE is coded as UVCF, how is FILM coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one step forward: F→G, I→J, L→M, M→N.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A is the sister of B. C is the mother of B. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: A is C's daughter and C is D's daughter, so A is D's granddaughter.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A man is facing North. He turns 90° clockwise, then 180°, and then 90° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: North → (90° clockwise) East → (180°) West → (90° anticlockwise) South.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All radiographers are technicians. Some technicians are doctors. Conclusions: I. Some radiographers are doctors.  II. All technicians are radiographers.
questions.explanation: The doctors may lie among technicians who are not radiographers, so I does not follow. 'All radiographers are technicians' cannot be reversed, so II does not follow.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is about:
questions.explanation: 7.9 km/s is the orbital velocity near the Earth's surface; 11.2 km/s is the escape velocity.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Isotopes of an element have:
options: The same mass number but different atomic numbers
The same atomic number but different mass numbers
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ only in the number of neutrons, e.g., C-12 and C-14, or Tc-99 and Tc-99m (an isomer).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which blood cells help in the clotting of blood?
questions.explanation: Platelets form a plug and release clotting factors.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas is released during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (in sunlight, with chlorophyll).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate; washing soda is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Two resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human somatic cell?
questions.explanation: 23 pairs: 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives an erect, diminished image with a wide field of view.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which inert gas is filled in electric bulbs to prolong the life of the filament?
questions.explanation: Argon reduces evaporation of the tungsten filament and does not react with it.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which enzyme present in saliva begins the digestion of starch?
questions.explanation: Ptyalin converts starch into maltose in the mouth.
